newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas prices soften on weather, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices soften on weather, NYMEX.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for June 1 drifted lower Thursday to converge with next-day values as milder weather in western Canada weakened demand and the futures market faltered, industry sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for June 1 delivery slid about five cents to the high-C$1.50s per gigajoule, while next-day prices were quoted at C$1.56-1.57.
Temperatures in Calgary, Alberta, were forecast to reach highs around 70 degrees F today, followed by a high of about 60 degrees on Friday, Weather Services Corp reported.
July Hub futures fell to a low of $2.24, down 7.6 cents.
NYMEX also pressured Niagara prices into the low-to-mid $2.40s per million British thermal units (mmBtu), traders said, indicating a gain of about five cents from May 1 levels.
At Sumas, Wash., June 1 gas traded at $1.23-1.27 per mmBtu, down five to 10 cents from May indices.
